details:
After visiting certain sequences of worlds or viewing avatars in PCVR, VRChat enters a persistent degraded state. Worlds that normally run smoothly become dramatically slower, and restarting VRChat restores performance. Moving to a lighter world can make the problem less noticeable, but returning similar worlds exposes it again. Seems to be triggered by worlds or avatars with heavy shader usage.

I have experienced this on two identical systems, using both Steam Link and Virtual Desktop. I have not seen the same problem in desktop mode. Lowering SteamVR resolution and shadow settings has not materially improved the severe state.

I initially investigated this using a longer sequence of world visits that I have trace logs for. Shared below is some data from my captures in Pokemon Pocket TCG, where the collapse was most pronounced. I have since narrowed this down to the shorter specific route below, which reproduces the collapse every time I have tried it: 100% reproduction. This shorter route provides a quicker way to reproduce the issue documented by those earlier captures.

HOW TO REPRODUCE

The sequence seems to matter for some reason.

In one PCVR session, visit these worlds in order without restarting VRChat:

1. Displace -launch into here as homeworld

   https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_59e75193-4507-4064-8dd7-ad7fa9de717f

2. OT&T Penthouse

   https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_3fc26f42-ce27-47cb-9ec0-a03330306809

3. The first of the month

   https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_c9ceb2f9-1bd2-4a74-96a9-5bb9d3f34d18

4. Abandoned Mall

   https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_1d65dbb4-cd63-4ccb-86b6-04368a88d087

In Abandoned Mall, respawn until you appear in the Food Court. Rotate so the entrance is on your right, then enable the VRChat personal mirror. At this point, my frame rate drops to approximately 15 FPS. (about half what it is in a fresh restart)

You can continue to Pokemon Pocket TCG to see the persistent slowdown there:

https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_3faab157-32cd-4706-b2b9-d92e4ba8130d

The mirror makes the collapse easy to see in Abandoned Mall. The severe slowdown is very apparent in Pokemon, which was used for benchmark captures.

Expected: Returning to the same scene, viewpoint and settings after visiting other worlds should give comparable performance.

Actual: Affected scenes and many following worlds remain severely slower until I restart VRChat.

BEFORE/AFTER CAPTURE EVIDENCE

My saved captures document Pokemon Pocket TCG before and after the longer world-hopping sequence, rather than the newly shortened route. Earlier fresh-client checks in this world were approximately 105–116 FPS, compared with approximately 15 FPS in the degraded state, alone with mirrors off.

Analysis of seven retained seconds from each capture shows:

Measurement                                                             GOOD          BAD

Render-thread CPU samples containing Map          0.64%        86.14%

Samples at the NVIDIA polling instruction                31         4,049

Average GPU power                                                   169 W          63 W

Average GPU graphics clock                                      2.34 GHz      2.74 GHz

In plain terms, the CPU thread responsible for rendering spends much of its sampled time repeatedly checking a condition inside the graphics driver while trying to update rendering data. This appears to hold up useful rendering work reaching the GPU, which fits the GPU drawing much less power despite maintaining high clocks. The waiting is visible on the CPU side inside the driver; the traces have not identified the condition it is waiting for.

The same Map/polling pattern appears throughout the degraded capture and in earlier captures. This identifies where progress is being lost once the collapse occurs. It does not yet identify which earlier action creates the state, the exact buffer involved, or whether the underlying fault is in VRChat, Unity or the driver.

TECHNICAL DETAILS

The sampled path is UnityPlayer -> D3D11 Map -> nvwgf2umx. Static analysis of the matching UnityPlayer binary identifies a dynamic, CPU-write constant-buffer update path. 

For the captured binaries:

- D3D11 Map stack offset: d3d11.dll+0x165651.

- UnityPlayer caller return RVAs include +0x8e5150, +0x8e525c and +0x8ec17c.

- NVIDIA hot sampled instruction: nvwgf2umx.dll+0x59886e, in a polling loop containing PAUSE at +0x59886c.

ENVIRONMENT FOR THE CAPTURES

- Lenovo Legion Pro 7 16AFR10H, type 83RU

- AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX3D; NVIDIA RTX 5080 Laptop GPU, 16 GB VRAM; 32 GB RAM

- VRChat 2026.4.1-1935-a61ceb9d89-Release, Steam open-beta branch (happens on main too)

- Unity 6000.0.67f1-DWR; Direct3D 11

- NVIDIA 610.62 / Windows driver 32.0.16.1062 (recommended Virtual Desktop driver. Happens on modern last checked)

- Windows 11 Pro, build 10.0.26300; SteamVR 2.18.4

- Steam Link for the matched captures
title: [1935]Severe, persistent PCVR performance collapse after changing worlds or avatars — reproducible route
